::: {#exr-piecewise}
## A piecewise function

::: {.lm-solution}
1. Both pieces are continuous; at $x = 1$, the left piece gives $1$, the right one tends to $a - 1$. So $f$ is continuous for $a = 2$.

1. Yes: the derivative of the left piece at $1$ is $2 \cdot 1 = 2$, that of the right piece is $a = 2$.
:::
:::

::: {#exr-bisection}
## Bisection

### Implementation

::: {.lm-solution}
The function is in `src/bisection.jl` (see the appendix).
:::

### Errors

::: {.lm-solution}
```{julia}
midpoints = bisection(x -> cos(x) - x, 0.0, 1.0, 40)
midpoints[end]
```

After $n$ steps, the interval has the length $2^{-n}$. Ten correct digits need $2^{-n} < 10^{-10}$, that is $n \geq 34$.
:::
:::

::: {#exr-bisection-speed}
## How fast does bisection converge?

```{julia}
#| include: true
errors = abs.(bisection(x -> cos(x) - x, 0.0, 1.0, 10) .- 0.7390851332151607)
```

::: {.lm-solution}
On average by $2$, as the interval is halved in each step. Single steps may do better or worse, depending on where the midpoint falls.
:::
:::

## Appendix

### `src/bisection.jl`

```{.julia .number-lines}
# The midpoints of the first n intervals of bisection for a zero of f in [a, b].
function bisection(f, a, b, n)
    midpoints = Float64[]
    for k in 1:n
        m = (a + b) / 2
        push!(midpoints, m)
        if sign(f(m)) == sign(f(a))
            a = m
        else
            b = m
        end
    end
    return midpoints
end
```
